To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the frequency of chromosome aberrations (CA) is increased in workers occupationally exposed to organic solvers, (ii) this frequency is influenced by polymorphisms of xenobiotic-methabolism and DNA-repair genes, (iii) these polymorphisms can be used as biomarkers of susceptibility and (iv) these biomarkers can be used to predict the frequency of CA in individuals exposed to organic solvants.
the chromosome aberrations frequency in lymphocytes was influenced by polymorphisms in the genes CYP2E, GSTM1, GSTT1, XRCC1 and XRCC3 in workers exposed to a mixture of organic solvents.

we found a significant increase in the chromosome aberration (CA) frequency in car painters exposed to organic solvent and the polymorphic genotyping in the genes XRCC1, CYP2E, XRCC3, GSTT1 and GSTM1 influenced CA frequency in the exposed workers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a significant increase in the CA frequency in exposed subjects and the influence of genetic polymorphisms in CYP2E, GSTM, GSTT, XRCC1 and XRCC3.
the development of new tools to reduce the health risks associated with occupational organic solvents exposure.
the development of new tools for the evaluation of occupational health risks and the implementation of preventive strategies in countries where organic solvents are not regulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in this particular study, the GSTM1 null, XRCC1 194 Arg/Trp and XRCC3 241 Thr/Thr polymorphic genotypes, and the wild genotypes of CYP2E 1, GSTT1, XRCC1 (280) Arg/arg and XRCC1 (399) Arg/Arg, are associated with an increased risk of CAs in workers exposed to solvents.

, the presence of GSTM1 null, XRCC1 (194) Arg/Arg or Arg/Trp and XRCC1 (280) Arg/arg genotypes, and XRCC1 241 Thr/Thr genotype are associated with an increased CA frequency in workers exposed to solvents, suggesting a higher risk of genetic damage.
the use of organic solvents is a risk factor for CA induction in workers and that polymorphic genotypes are associated with increased CA frequency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of individual susceptibility markers, such as polymorphisms in genes of xenobiotic-matabolism and DNA repair, is useful for the follow-up of workers exposed to organic solvent and for the development of preventive strategies to reduce the health risks.

the use of organic solvents in developing countries should be restricted to those cases in which they cannot be replaced by other products and that workers should be provided with appropriate protection equipment and training.
the polymorphisms of the genes XRCC1, XRCC3, CYP2E and GSTM1, GSTT1 could be used to identify individuals at higher risk for CA frequency in workers exposed to low concentrations of organic solvents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
occupational exposure to organic solvents is a significant CA risk factor, which can be influenced by the presence of polymorphisms.
we provide a new tool for occupational surveillance and prevention of potential health risk in countries with a high population of car painters and limited organic solvent use control.
the combination of genetic polymorphisms and exposure can help to predict the risk of chromosome aberrations in workers.
